solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Funny character securing lids, I forget the name

indicators.note: a thing that secures another holds it fast inside, so one piece is wrapped round the other

parts.note: a funny character is a WIT, a person given to jokes
lids is slang for HATS

explanation.surface: A comedian keeps a grip on some lids, then admits to forgetting what they are called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I forget the name' looks like the speaker's aside but is the definition: the phrase a speaker uses for a thing whose name escapes them.
explanation.definitionFit: A whatsit is a placeholder word used for an object whose proper name a speaker cannot recall.

clue.text: Buffalo (as American might say) following with clumsy gait

indicators.note: following means coming after, so one piece is placed after the other

parts.note: buffalo is a North American verb for bewilder, which is ADDLE

explanation.surface: A buffalo lumbers along in the American way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffalo' is a verb here: Chambers gives it as North American for bewilder or confuse, which is to ADDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A waddle is the swaying, short-stepped walk of a duck or a heavy person.

clue.text: A matelot, reportedly offensive

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the sound of the word stands in for its spelling

parts.note: a matelot is a sailor, an old salt, so this phrase is 'a salt'

explanation.surface: A sailor is said to be rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A salt', a sailor, said aloud gives the answer. 'offensive' is a noun: a military attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An offensive is an attack, which is what an assault is.

clue.text: Character whose skin breaks to make silk

indicators.note: one word breaks another when it splits it open and sits inside

parts.note: silk is made by spinning, so SPIN
derma is the skin

explanation.surface: A superhero whose skin bursts to produce silk.
explanation.walkthrough: The comic-book hero shoots webs from wrist devices, not silk from his skin, so the surface is a tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Spider-Man is a Marvel comic-book character, a superhero with spider powers.

clue.text: "Stop! The line's busy", might one say?

definitions.text: "Stop! The line's busy", might one say?

indicators.note: busy means bustling and restless, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone at a switchboard barking that the line is engaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' rearranges STOP THE LINE, and the whole clue is what such a person might say.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephonist operates a switchboard and would tell callers that a line is engaged.

clue.text: Singular, small flower pots for flower

indicators.note: to pot a plant is to set it in a container, so the first flower here holds the other letters

parts.note: a flower is a BLOOM
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A gardener's note about a single small bloom being put into pots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pots' is the containment signal: BLOOM holds the two S letters to give BLO-SS-OM. The final 'flower' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Blossom is the bloom of a fruit tree or shrub, a straightforward synonym for a flower.

clue.text: Malicious smear turning up

indicators.note: in a down answer turning up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to dab is to smear lightly

explanation.surface: A spiteful smear campaign resurfaces.
explanation.walkthrough: DAB reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad can mean wicked or malicious, as in bad intentions.

clue.text: Official publication that's stopped

definitions.meaning: a newspaper or journal speaking for a party or body
a church ... has stops, so it is a thing that is stopped

explanation.surface: A government newspaper that has ceased printing.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a body's mouthpiece journal, and the musical instrument is fitted with stops controlling its pipes.

clue.text: Pull up towels, bandaging a black cormorant, say?

indicators.note: bandaging wraps round, so the turned word encloses the next pieces
in a down answer pulling up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to towel is to dry, so towels gives DRIES
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: Someone hauls up towels and binds an oil-blackened cormorant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull up' makes SEIRD, which 'bandaging' wraps round the next letters. A cormorant is one example, hence 'say?'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cormorant is a fish-eating bird of coasts and seas, one example of a marine bird.

clue.text: Welcomed into government department, comforting word appeared caring?

indicators.note: being welcomed into somewhere means going inside it, so one piece sits in the other

parts.note: MOD is the UK Ministry of Defence
there is said to soothe, as in 'there, there'

explanation.surface: A minister welcomed to a department, with soothing words, seemed caring.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ministry of Defence is a British government department; 'there, there' is what one says to soothe a child.
explanation.definitionFit: To mother is to look after protectively, so someone who mothered behaved in a nurturing, caring way.

clue.text: Checked out bottles all the same, such as whisky?

indicators.note: to bottle something is to enclose it, so one word holds the other within

parts.note: to check out is slang for to die, so DIED
all the same means nevertheless, which is STILL

explanation.surface: Someone inspects bottled spirits and finds them identical, whisky included.
explanation.walkthrough: DIED holds STILL to give DI-STILL-ED. A whisky is given as an example of a distilled drink, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky is made by distillation, so it is an example of a distilled spirit.

clue.text: General entitlement

definitions.meaning: Ulysses S. ... was the Union general in the American Civil War
a sum or right given to someone, something they are entitled to

explanation.surface: A general sense of entitlement, as of someone spoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Grant names a famous American general, and also an award or allowance one is entitled to.

clue.text: Insect in river adjoining lake

indicators.note: adjoining means placed right beside, so the two pieces are set side by side

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
the Ouse is an English river, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A bug found in a river next to a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The OUSE is a river in England (there are several). Put L beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A louse is a small wingless parasitic insect.

clue.text: Game not applicable: is English dance?

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
NA is the abbreviation for not applicable, as on forms

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether something is an English dance rather than a game.
explanation.walkthrough: A charade of POLO, NA, IS and E. The polonaise is in fact Polish, which may be the point of the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The polonaise is a stately processional dance of Polish origin.

clue.text: If sister wrongly following boy — what should he have said?

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the scrambled letters come after the boy

parts.note: a boy is a LAD

indicators.note: wrongly means in the wrong order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy pushes ahead of his sister, and is asked what he should have said.
explanation.walkthrough: LAD, then 'wrongly' turns IF SISTER into IESFIRST.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Ladies first' is the polite phrase a gentleman says when letting women go ahead of him.

clue.text: Battle ground

definitions.meaning: the Battle of ... in 1066 saw Harold defeat the Norwegian invaders
The London football ground of Chelsea FC

explanation.surface: Just two words: a fight and a field.
explanation.walkthrough: Stamford Bridge is both a Yorkshire battle site from 1066 and the home stadium of Chelsea, a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a historic English battle and to a well-known football stadium.

clue.text: Switch back on cooker

parts.note: the back of something is its REAR
a range is a large kitchen stove

explanation.surface: Turning a switch back on at the cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch back on' reads like turning a cooker on again; 'Switch' is the definition and 'on' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch things is to change their order or arrangement, which is to rearrange them.

clue.text: Dollar maybe, outstanding, surged

parts.note: a dollar bill is a BILL, a banknote
an outstanding debt is one still OWED

explanation.surface: A dollar, perhaps exceptional, shot up in value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' looks like praise but means unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoke or sails that billowed swelled out and rolled in waves, as a sea surges.

clue.text: Insincere old eccentric packaging up a book token

indicators.note: packaging something up wraps it round, so the scrambled letters enclose the other piece
eccentric means odd or irregular, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cynical old oddball wraps a book token, and does not mean it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' makes INCONSIDERLE, which 'packaging up' wraps round the rest. 'token' is the definition, an adjective, as in a token gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: A token amount is a trivial or negligible one, just as an inconsiderable sum is.

clue.text: Well-dressed boy in yellow

parts.note: chic means stylish and well dressed
Ken is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A smart young man in a yellow outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in yellow' reads like clothing; 'yellow' is the definition, meaning cowardly, and 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow and chicken are both slang adjectives for cowardly.

clue.text: Boat now free of freight?

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed barge for ferrying cargo
a vessel unloaded is ... than before

explanation.surface: A boat which has just been unloaded.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a cargo barge, and anything that has shed its load weighs less.

clue.text: After uprising, imperial award stuck in throat for online observer

indicators.note: in a down answer an uprising reads from the bottom up, so the whole is backwards
stuck in means lodged inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a maw is a gullet or throat
CBE is Commander of the Order of the British Empire, an honour

explanation.surface: An honour from the Empire sticks in someone's craw after a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck in' gives MACBEW, which 'After uprising' turns upwards in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A webcam is a camera streaming images over the internet, a watcher on the web.

clue.text: Second cracking title surprisingly providing theme

indicators.note: something cracking another breaks into it, so it sits inside the other
surprisingly suggests the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: a MO is a moment or second, as in 'half a mo'
providing (that) means IF

explanation.surface: A second-place finisher breaks through to a title, surprisingly, which becomes the theme of the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' makes LEITT, and 'cracking' gives LEITMOT before the final piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A leitmotif is a recurring theme in music or literature, associated with a character or idea.

clue.text: Meat that's new devoured by rodents

indicators.note: being devoured means being swallowed inside, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: mice are rodents

explanation.surface: Fresh meat eaten by rats or mice.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside MICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mince is minced meat, beef chopped finely.

clue.text: Straying inside Cairo guesthouse

indicators.note: inside says the answer lies within the run of letters of the next words

explanation.surface: Wandering about inside a guesthouse in Cairo.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across CaiRO GUEsthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue animal is one that has strayed from its herd and wanders alone, often dangerous.

clue.text: After heart transplant, females returned to conscious state

indicators.note: a heart transplant swaps the organ at the centre, so the middle letter of the word is exchanged for another

parts.note: females are WOMEN

explanation.surface: Patients recover consciousness after their heart operations.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is literal: the heart (middle letter) of WOMEN, M, is swapped for a new one, K. The new letter has no source in the clue; the answer settles it.
explanation.definitionFit: Woken is the past participle of wake, meaning brought or come back out of sleep into awareness.

clue.text: Turn of the prince to be very agitated, once

indicators.note: a turn of letters twists them about into a new order

explanation.surface: A prince's tantrum, a royal turn from an earlier age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn of' rearranges THE PRINCE. 'once' marks this as an old spelling of frenetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrenetic is an archaic form of frenetic, meaning frantic or wildly excited.

clue.text: Fastener that's long made slightly shorter

indicators.note: slightly shorter means losing just a little at the end, here the last letter

parts.note: to long for something is to PINE

explanation.surface: A long fastener trimmed a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' reads as an adjective but is the verb PINE, which loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin is a small pointed fastener for holding cloth or paper together.

clue.text: Waste time in oubliette

parts.note: dung is animal waste
an eon (aeon) is a vast stretch of time

explanation.surface: Wasting time locked away in a pit of a prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waste' reads as a verb but supplies DUNG, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An oubliette is a secret dungeon reached only through a trapdoor in its ceiling.

clue.text: Yours truly repelled by the golden rule

indicators.note: by means beside, so the turned piece stands next to the others

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the letters face the other way

parts.note: yours truly is the speaker, ME

explanation.surface: The speaker rejects the golden rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repelled' turns the speaker round to EM; 'golden rule' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a proposition established as a general principle, a rule proved from axioms.
